column1: # PLACES -- REFERENCE. Identity and the distances between them.
# *** THIS FILE KILLS TWO LIVE ERRORS. ***
# 1. WETHERBY / WETHERSBY. Both spellings are in this repository, some of them
#    typed by the player, and until now nothing reconciled them. `aliases` makes
#    them one town. A validator can then refuse a row naming a place that does
#    not exist, which a fuzzy match never could.
# 2. THE DISTANCE TABLE LIVED IN `calendar.md` PROSE AND WAS MISQUOTED. The DM
#    twice described the cart as "a day behind at Fenn's" when Ede's gate is
#    EIGHT MILES from Fenn's yard -- a couple of hours, not a day. A cart out of
#    Fenn's is at Ede's door before dinner.
# *** THE TRUE MAP. POSITIONS ARE EXACT. ***
# x_ft = feet EAST of Wethersby, y_ft = feet NORTH. FEET, because that is what
# the dungeon already uses (10-ft squares), so campaign/frames.tsv can put a
# corridor square and a stretch of road in ONE coordinate system.
# THERE IS NO UNCERTAINTY COLUMN HERE, AND THAT IS THE POINT. The world is
# where it is; Wethersby does not move. What is uncertain is what the PARTY
# KNOWS, and that lives in campaign/knowledge.tsv where it belongs. An earlier
# draft carried a precision_ft here and the player caught it: it was measuring
# the DM's doubt about his own reading of the narrative, which is a property of
# neither the world nor the party.
# SCALE IS THE BOOK'S, NOT A GUESS: rules/overland.md, DMG p.58. Cart on a road
# 25 mi/day, laden walk 20, medium mount 40. An earlier draft used a
# DM-invented 18 mi/day for CARTS, reasoned off a WALKING figure -- so Marchford
# has moved from 54 miles to 75 and Ludbury from 90 to 125. EVERY TRAVEL TIME IN
# THE NARRATIVE IS UNCHANGED, because the times are what was played; only the
# mileage moved, and it moved onto the book.
# `attested_days` + `attested_mode` are THE NARRATIVE'S OWN CLAIM, kept so that
# `overland.py check` can compare the model against it. That is not a second
# copy of one fact -- it is the claim and the model, and deleting the claim
# would leave nothing able to catch the model drifting.
# `fix`: attested (bearing AND distance in the record) | part (one of them) |
# call (NEITHER -- placed to make the map work, and NOT CANON: if play fixes a
# position, play wins) | region (an area, not a point).
# `established_day` is the campaign day play pinned it. Blank if it never has.
# NORTH. ONE DAY BY CART = 18 MILES, which is the attested figure and not a
# guess: the crag turning is "one day's walk, call it fifteen to twenty miles
# laden". `tools/overland.py check` recomputes every distance off these
# coordinates and FAILS if the grid stops agreeing with the travel times the
# narrative has already used -- so the map cannot quietly drift from the
# fiction, which is the whole reason it is data and not a picture.
# `fix` says how the position was arrived at, because that distinction is
# load-bearing and a map hides it better than prose does:
#   attested  bearing AND distance are both in the record
#   part      one of the two is; the other is a DM call
#   call      NEITHER is on record. Placed to make the schematic work
#   region    an area, not a point
# `days_from_wethersby` is BY CART unless the note says otherwise, because a
# cart is what the party moves goods with. Riding times are in the note where
# they differ and matter -- Draycot is a long day's RIDE and two days' walk, and
# that difference has already decided a scene.
# Blank means not established. Blank is honest; a guessed distance would be
# quoted back as a fact, which is how the Fenn's/Ede's error happened.
